{{short description|American astrophysicist and cosmologist (born 1947)}}
'''Edward L. (Ned) Wright''' (born August 25, 1947, in [[Washington, D.C.]]) is an American [[astrophysicist]] and [[cosmologist]]. He has worked on space missions including the [[Cosmic Background Explorer]] (COBE), [[Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer]] (WISE), and [[Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe]] (WMAP) projects.

Wright received his ABscl (Physics in 1969) and [[PhD]] (Astronomy in 1976) degrees in high-altitude rocket measurement of the cosmic microwave background radiation from [[Harvard University]], where he was a [[Harvard Society of Fellows|junior fellow]]. After teaching as a tenured associate professor in the [[MIT]] Physics Department for a while, Wright has been a professor at [[UCLA]] since 1981.<ref>{{cite web | title =  Ned Wright's web page at UCLA | url = http://www.astro.ucla.edu/~wright/intro.html}}</ref>

Wright researches [[infrared astronomy]] and cosmology. He has studied [[fractal]] dust grains which are able to [[Absorption spectroscopy|absorb and emit]] efficiently at millimeter [[wavelength]]s, and other aspects that may be important factors in understanding the [[cosmic microwave background]]. As an interdisciplinary scientist on the Space InfraRed Telescope Facility ([[Spitzer Space Telescope|SIRTF]]) Science Working Group,<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.spitzer.caltech.edu/features/p_nedwright.shtml |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20060623092949/http://www.spitzer.caltech.edu/features/p_nedwright.shtml |archivedate = 2006-06-23 | title = SIRTF Profiles: Ned Wright | accessdate = 2010-01-26}}</ref> Wright began working on the SIRTF project (renamed the Spitzer Space Telescope) in 1976. He was an active member of the teams working on the Cosmic Background Explorer (COBE) beginning in 1978. He is the principal investigator on the Wide field Infrared Survey Explorer ([[Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer|WISE]]) project.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/WISE/mission/index.html | title = WISE: Mission Overview | publisher = [[NASA]] | accessdate = 2010-01-26 | archive-date = 2019-09-03 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190903234237/https://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/WISE/mission/index.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> Wright is also a member of the current science team on the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe ([[WMAP]]), which was launched in June 2001. WMAP followed up the COBE discovery of early fluctuations in the developing [[Universe]].

From 1994 to 1998, he served as a science editor of ''[[The Astrophysical Journal]]''.

==Honors and awards==
* [[NASA]] Exceptional Scientific Achievement Medal for his work on COBE, in 1992.<ref name='nap'>{{cite book | title = NASA's Beyond Einstein Program: An Architecture for Implementation | year=2007 | url = http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=12006&page=172 |isbn=978-0-309-11162-1 | page = 172 |publisher =[[National Academies Press]]| doi=10.17226/12006 }}</ref>
* Named the [[CSEOL]] Distinguished Scientist of the Year, in 1995.
* Elected to the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name="nas">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/edward-l-wright-tlf29a/|access-date=2013-11-02|work=National Academy of Sciences|title=Edward L. Wright}}</ref>
* [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]], December 2017<ref>{{cite web |url=https://science.gsfc.nasa.gov/sed/index.cfm?fuseAction=home.main&&navOrgCode=660 |title=Congratulations to Charles Bennett, Gary Hinshaw, Norman Jarosik, Lyman Page Jr., David Spergel and the WMAP Science Team for winning the 2018 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=3 December 2017 |website=science.gsfc.nasa.gov |publisher=[[NASA]] |access-date=8 December 2017}}</ref>
